messages:
Carla M.: Heads-up — started seeing p95 latency jump on shared-gpu pool `south-2` ~ 22:40 UTC. Baseline p95 ~80ms, now ~950ms. Affected tenant mix looks like mixed long-seq + short-chat.
Omar N.: Noted. Any spikes in batch size / kernel changes around the same time? I’ll pull the kernel selection logs.
Carla M.: I see a correlated spike at 22:39 in `batch_size` distribution: sudden tail of batches ~512 tokens. Also a kernel switch event to `kern_v2_int8` coincidentally.
InfraBot: alert: latency_spike detected on pool-south-2 — p95 950ms (+>10x). triggered at 2201234568
Omar N.: Quick dump of kernel selector trace:
```
2026-03-17T22:39:12Z selector: tenant=acme-prod batch_median=48 batch_tail=512 -> selected=kern_v2_int8 reason=throughput_hint
2026-03-17T22:39:12Z runtime: kern_v2_int8 latency_ms=820 p95
2026-03-17T22:39:13Z runtime: kern_v1_fp16 latency_ms=110 p95 (for smaller batches)
```
Omar N.: Looks like the selector prioritized throughput and chose v2 int8 for large batches but that kernel has worse short-latency characteristics on mixed seq sizes.
Sophia L.: I’m seeing KV cache miss-rate spike for tenant `acme-prod` at the same time — cache warmup from recent long-run job. Misses -> more KV fetches -> larger prefixes -> batches coalesce.
Jin K.: Repro hypothesis: a noisy tenant (long-seq RLHF run) saturated batch queue, heuristic aggregated mixed short requests into huge batches. Kernel chosen for those large batches is optimized for long homogeneous seqs but hurts mixed workloads. Also KV thrash means more mem copies.
Carla M.: So root cause candidate: bursty long-seq tenant caused batching heuristic to make huge batches, kernel autoswitch selected a throughput-optimized kernel that regresses p95 for mixed short requests, combined with KV miss amplification from priming.
Omar N.: Quick mitigation suggestion:
- clamp per-tenant max_batch_size to 128 (temp)
- add rate-shaping for long-seq tenants to smooth enqueueing
- pin hot KV keys for acme-prod for 15m
Carla M.: Can we patch selector to prefer latency-optimized kernel when batch contains >10% short requests? Even a fast rollback rule would help.
Jin K.: I can push a hotfix rule to selector config now: if short_request_ratio > 0.1 -> prefer kern_v1_fp16. Rolling to 10% of nodes in pool south-2.
InfraBot: deploy: kernel-selector-config rollout started (10%) by Jin K. at 2201234578
Sophia L.: I’ll run a targeted KV prewarm for acme-prod and monitor miss-rate.
Carla M.: Thanks. Short plan: (1) Jin rolls selector config -> monitor p95, (2) Sophia prewarm KV, (3) Omar and I watch for regressions, (4) if still bad, migrate noisy tenant to dedicated reserved capacity. Please post p95 numbers in this thread.
Omar N.: After 10% rollout: p95 down to ~220ms, KV miss-rate reduced 30% after prewarm.
Carla M.: Good start. Rollout to 50% if numbers hold. Add follow-up ticket to revisit batching heuristic — we need fairness-aware batching (per-tenant credit buckets) and a stronger kernel cost model.
Jin K.: Created ticket INF-3491: "fairshare batching + kernel-cost-model". Assigned to eng-runtime. ETA draft next-week.
Carla M.: :thumbsup: closing loop here — will update if anything changes.
